history.summary: A dedicated shrine of Narasimha Swamy located on Krosuru Road, Dharanikota, Amaravathi (522020), Palnadu district. Map listings confirm its existence and location, but no documented history (period, builder/dynasty, legend, renovation dates) could be found for this specific shrine in available sources. It is geographically distinct from the famous Lakshmi Narasimha temples of Mangalagiri (hill-top Panakala and downhill Diguva shrines), which lie roughly 27-28 km to the east in Guntur district.

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Amaravathi (also spelt Amaravati) is an ancient town on the southern bank of the Krishna River in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh. Known historically as Dhanyakataka or Dharanikota, it was a capital of the Satavahana dynasty and a major Buddhist centre, home to the great Amaravati mahachaitya (stupa). It is also the site of the Amareswara Temple, one of the five Pancharama Kshetras, while the adjoining ancient settlement of Dharanikota lies immediately to the west of the town.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (approx. 60 km from Amaravathi town).
travel.railway: Guntur Railway Station (approx. 34 km from Amaravathi town).
travel.road: APS RTC buses connect Amaravathi bus stand (approx. 4-5 km away) with Guntur, Vijayawada and Mangalagiri; local autos/taxis cover the last mile. The temple is on Krosuru Road, Dharanikota, just west of Amaravathi town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February is generally the most pleasant season in coastal Andhra (verify for this shrine).
